title: Tiered Degradation Policy and Incident Runbook
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a tiered degradation policy for Redwood inference services, prescribes how SLOs and error budgets drive automated and manual fallbacks, and provides a single consolidated incident runbook for latency and capacity incidents. It is intended for SREs, service owners, on-call engineers, and incident commanders.

Scope: Applies to externally-facing inference endpoints and internal model routing services (gateway, router, and batch workers). Does not change product-level feature flags; it controls operational fallbacks and capacity actions.

Key goals:
- Preserve customer-facing availability for critical endpoints at acceptable latencies.
- Constrain error-budget consumption and provide deterministic throttles.
- Provide clear, repeatable decision steps and ownership for incidents involving SLO regressions, capacity exhaustion, and cascading degradations.

Definitions
- SLO: Service Level Objective; the signed SLA-derived internal objectives used for operational decisioning.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (e.g., 99.5% success yields 0.5% error budget).
- Burn rate: rate at which error budget is being consumed relative to expected pace.
- Degradation tier: pre-defined operational posture (Tier 0, Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3).

SLOs and Error Budgets (examples)

Primary SLOs (per-customer route)
| Metric | SLO target | Measurement window | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Successful responses (4xx/5xx filtered) | 99.5% | 30d rolling | Service owner | Threshold used for monthly SLA alignment |
| p99 latency (inference + routing) | <= 1200ms | 7d rolling | Runtime team | p95 target at 200ms for free-tier; p99 for committed capacity |
| Embeddings throughput (tokens/sec) | >= configured baseline | 1d rolling | Dedicated capacity team | Applies to Dedicated pools only |

Error budget policy
- Full error budget = 1 - SLO. For the 99.5% SLO, error budget = 0.5%.
- Burn-rate windows monitored: 1h, 6h, 24h.
- Trigger thresholds (automatic alarms):
  1. Advisory: burn rate > 2x over 6h => notify oncall via Slack and paging channel.
  2. Constrained: burn rate > 5x over 1h => initiate Tier 1 actions (see Degradation tiers).
  3. Critical: burn rate > 10x over 1h or sustained 5x over 6h => escalate to incident commander and prepare customer communications.

Degradation tiers (operational posture)
- Tier 0 (Normal): No automatic degradation. Auto-scaling active.
- Tier 1 (Constrained): Non-critical work deprioritized. Apply request shaping and priority queueing. Route to cached KV responses when available.
- Tier 2 (Moderate degradation): Drop non-essential routes and reduce max tokens per request for best-effort plans. Shift non-committed customers to lower-cost model variants.
- Tier 3 (Broad degradation / Emergency): Graceful fallback to queued processing / synthetic responses; begin global throttling and enable broad circuit breakers. Notify customers.

Decision matrix (summary)
- Burn rate 2–5x and p95 latency < 800ms => Tier 1.
- Burn rate 5–10x or p95 latency 800–1200ms => Tier 2.
- Burn rate >10x or p99 latency > 2000ms or sustained queue growth => Tier 3.

Capacity planning and surge playbook
1. Forecasting and guardrails
   - Maintain a 30% buffer on committed Dedicated pools for peak windows (customer-defined).
   - Maintain a rolling 14-day forecast of token volume per region and per model.
   - Define model-specific headroom multipliers: default x1.5 for low variance models, x2.5 for high variance (RLHF/chatty) models.

2. Emergency scaling options (ordered by preference)
   1. Activate reserved burst capacity for affected pool (automated, if policy allows).
   2. Trigger autoscaler to add pre-warmed nodes (expected time to readiness: 90–180s).
   3. Route lower-priority tenants to overflow pools with quantized models.
   4. Enable short-lived CPU-backed fallback workers for small requests (latency trade-off).
   5. Regional failover to nearby region where capacity and compliance permit.

3. Runbook: sudden capacity spike (step-by-step)
   1. Pager: oncall receives alerts for burn rate and queue depth. Acknowledge within 2 minutes.
   2. Initial assessment (5 minutes): check dashboards ("SLO Overview", "Queue Depth", "Autoscaler Events", "Pool Utilization"). Confirm whether spike is traffic-driven, model-regression, or infrastructure failure.
   3. Assign incident roles: incident commander (IC), communications lead, runtime lead, capacity lead.
   4. If burn rate condition matches Tier 1 or higher, move to the applicable tier actions below.
   5. Apply immediate mitigations: reduce max_tokens per request by 20% for non-critical tenants, enable priority queueing, and increase sampling on tracing for the affected services.
   6. If autoscaler does not satisfy demand within 5 minutes, activate reserved burst capacity and notify capacity lead to validate pre-warmed nodes.

Operational tooling and observability
- Dashboards to monitor (minimum): SLO Overview, Error Budget Burn, Pool Utilization by region, p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap, Request queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, Autoscaler Event log.
- Suggested alerting thresholds:
  - error_budget.burn_rate_1h > 5x => Pager (P1).
  - queue_depth > 1000 per pool for > 2 minutes => Pager (P1).
  - p99_latency > 2000ms for 5m => Pager (P1).
  - cache_hit_ratio < 20% for 10m (when cache expected) => Pager (P2).
- Tools and integrations:
  - Telemetry: OpenTelemetry traces, Prometheus metrics, and Loki for logs.
  - APM: Jaeger for distributed traces of model serving ops.
  - Incident: PagerDuty for on-call, Slack channel #sre-incidents for coordination, Statuspage for external comms.

Runbook extracts (CLI snippets and examples)
- Check recent burn rates (Grafana link placeholder): curl -s "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/ds/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"queries": [{"refId":"A","expr":"error_budget:burn_rate:1h"}] }'

- Inspect autoscaler events (kubectl example):
  kubectl -n runtime get hpa -o wide --selector=app=model-runtime
  kubectl -n runtime describe hpa model-runtime-main

- Drain and replace pre-warmed nodes (when necessary):
  gcloud compute instances set-scheduling $NODE --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE
  kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Tiered actions (detailed)
- Tier 1 (Constrained) actions (owner: runtime lead)
  - Enable priority queueing: POST /admin/routes/priority?level=high (internal API).
  - Start 2x sampling on traces for affected models.
  - Notify product on potentially affected SLAs (template message included below).

- Tier 2 (Moderate degradation) actions (owner: IC + capacity lead)
  - Shift non-committed customers to backup, quantized model variants. API: PATCH /admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/model_binding -> {"binding":"quantized-4bit-v2"}
  - Reduce default max_tokens by 30% for public routes via feature toggle.
  - Engage support for targeted customer outreach for customers above 95th percentile spend.

- Tier 3 (Emergency) actions (owner: IC + exec oncall)
  - Global throttle: apply rate limits at the edge for best-effort traffic.
  - Disable streaming for low-tier requests and queue them for batch processing.
  - Publish external status with estimated mitigation ETA.

Customer communication templates (internal)
- Short status update (to publish on Statuspage and Slack):
  "We are investigating elevated latency impacting text-generation endpoints in region X. Our on-call team has initiated fallbacks; some requests may be delayed or throttled. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."

- Detailed post-incident summary fields (used by IC after containment):
  1. Incident summary (what happened)
  2. Impact (number of affected customers, % error budget consumed)
  3. Root cause (preliminary then confirmed)
  4. Timeline (events by minute)
  5. Actions taken during incident (mitigations and commands)
  6. Post-incident actions and owners

Incident review standards and RCA expectations
- Post-incident timeline: publish an initial incident review within 72 hours; final RCA and action plan within 14 days.
- RCA format must include: evidence links (traces, logs, dashboards), hypothesis testing steps, blast radius assessment, and cost/impact estimate.
- Severity taxonomy mapping:
  - Sev1: Multi-region customer-impacting latency or errors >3 hours or >25% customers impacted.
  - Sev2: Single-region customer-impacting performance for >30 minutes.
  - Sev3: Degraded non-customer-facing internal metrics or minor customer impacts.

Reliability initiatives and continuous improvement
- Quarterly exercises: capacity chaos tests that simulate 30–50% of pool churn and evaluate recovery within 10 minutes. Runbook owners must participate and provide a short report.
- SLO rehearse: monthly error-budget drills for high-variance models to validate tiered actions.
- Observability maturity: add synthetic traffic probes per region and per model; measure end-to-end latency and model quality regressions.

Rollout, ownership, and governance
- Ownership matrix:
  - Runtime lead: implement runtime-level throttles, autoscaler tuning.
  - Capacity lead: reserved capacity, pre-warm policies, cloud account quotas.
  - Oncall SRE: first responder and initial mitigation.
  - Incident commander: leads escalation and comms.
  - Product/security: consulted for customer-impacting or compliance-sensitive degradations.

- Governance: any change to tier thresholds or automatic throttle actions requires approval by the Reliability Council (runtime + platform + capacity) and one-week staged rollout with metrics validation.

Appendix: checklists and templates
1) Pre-incident checklist (oncall)\   - Verify telemetry ingestion is healthy.\   - Confirm alert routing and paging is operational.\   - Ensure access to admin APIs and runbook links.
2) Post-incident checklist (IC)\   - Confirm containment and rollback of temporary toggles.\   - Schedule RCA meeting and assign authors.\   - Raise follow-up tickets with owners and due dates.

3) Commands and links (placeholders)\   - SLO Overview dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/slo-overview\   - Pool Utilization: https://grafana.internal/redwood/pool-util
   - PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com

Appendix B: change log
- 2025-11-10: Initial draft created.
- 2025-12-05: Added burn-rate thresholds and tier definitions after tabletop exercise.
- 2026-01-15: Finalized CLI snippets, added customer comms templates, published.

End of document.
